topic: Law fact / myth-buster: posting your photo publicly on social media is not consent for anyone to misuse it in obscene material - Karnataka HC refuses to quash IT Act Sections 66C and 67 case; identity of person in video is for trial; no mini-trial in quashing plea (Dheeraj G Kunder & Others v. State of Karnataka, Crl. P. No. 16549 of 2025, 2026:KHC:57298, Justice Suraj Govindaraj, 12 Oct 2026)

slides.title: Your public photo is **not** free to misuse
slides.subtitle: Posting a photo on Instagram is **not consent** for anyone to use it in obscene content, says the Karnataka High Court.
slides.cite: **Dheeraj G Kunder & Others v. State of Karnataka** · Crl. P. No. 16549 of 2025 · 2026:KHC:57298 · Justice Suraj Govindaraj · 12 Oct 2026

slides.label: Myth 1
slides.title: "Public photo? **Free** to use"
bullets: **Fact:** the High Court said a photo being publicly available does **not**, by itself, give anyone the right to misuse it.
A photo posted for **ordinary, legitimate** reasons is not consent to use it in obscene material.
It is also not consent to **circulate** such material among others.

slides.label: What happened
slides.title: Her photos, an **obscene video**
bullets: A woman complained that her Instagram ID and photos were used with an **obscene video** shared in a WhatsApp group.
Her ID and contact details spread to more groups, and she began getting **unwanted messages**.
Police charge-sheeted five people under Sections **66C** (identity theft) and **67** (obscene material online) of the IT Act.

slides.label: Myth 2
slides.title: "Different face? **Case over**"
bullets: The accused argued the woman in the photos and the woman in the video were **different people**.
The court noted a forensic (FSL) report found **similar facial features**. Who is in the video is a question for **trial**.
A High Court cannot hold a **mini-trial** on a quashing plea. The petition was **dismissed**.
slides.note: **Law fact:** if proved, such conduct would expose a woman to humiliation, harassment and harm to her reputation, the court said.

slides.label: Keep in mind
slides.title: Case continues, **guilt not decided**
bullets: The court only refused to **quash** the case. The trial court must decide it **independently** on the evidence.
The forensic reports also recorded **limits**, such as not being able to tell whether files were edited.
This post is for information only, not legal advice.

slides.title: Know the law, know your **rights**
lines: One important legal update every day, in simple words.
**Save** this, and **share** it with friends who post photos online.

caption:
Posted your photo on Instagram? That does not give anyone the right to misuse it 📸⚖️

Myth: "If my photo is public, anyone can use it." The Karnataka High Court has said that a publicly available photo does not, by itself, allow another person to misuse it. A photo posted for ordinary and legitimate reasons cannot be treated as consent to use it in obscene material, or to pass such material around.

The case: a woman complained that her Instagram ID and photos were used with an obscene video shared in WhatsApp groups. Her ID and contact details spread further, and she started getting unwanted messages. Police filed a charge sheet against five people under Sections 66C (identity theft) and 67 (publishing obscene material electronically) of the IT Act.

The accused said the woman in the photos and the woman in the video were different people. The court noted that a forensic report found similar facial features, said this question must be decided at trial, and held that it cannot hold a mini-trial while deciding a quashing plea. The petition was dismissed. Remember, this does not mean anyone is guilty yet; the trial court will decide the case on the evidence.

Case: Dheeraj G Kunder & Others v. State of Karnataka, Crl. P. No. 16549 of 2025, 2026:KHC:57298
Bench: Justice Suraj Govindaraj, Karnataka High Court (order dated 12 Oct 2026)

This post is for information only, not legal advice.
